answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because voyage only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, thread is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
